title: The incident register, the two parameter codes and the right of the grant read are not specified for the break-glass slice
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-006); 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.28, AC-ALT-P4-009-01, AC-EXC-P4-007-01, AC-EXC-P4-007-02); 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T6.1, API-P4-013); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 14 and 20; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: (a) The open incident a grant is bound to has no owner, store, contract or reference pattern in any source of this read set: the legacy criterion needs an open incident and refuses a request without one, FSD P4 v3 A2.28 reaches Log Analytics and the Workbench and names no incident store, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no incident path and no event, so the check is a port with a Day-1 stub. (b) The two parameter codes behind the grant are named by no source, although the window hours and the reason floor are read as data: the window code and the reason-floor code are this key's own. (c) The legacy Permission checks table gives the story Platform administration R held by RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM and RW-SECADM, while TSD P4 v3 API-P4-013 declares right C for the activation, and the legacy Endpoints table gives only the access-log read that belongs to RWB-P4-E1039 and RWB-P4-AD007; the right of the grant read is therefore this revision's decision. (d) The legacy story says the grant lasts for the window and fixes no length; the four hours in force are taken from FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-009-01 and are carried as a parameter, never as a constant.
evidence: Legacy RWB-AD-006 story statement and AC1 to AC3; FSD P4 v3 A2.28 and AC-ALT-P4-009-01 (activation at 10:30, grant active until 14:30, group end 18:00) and AC-EXC-P4-007-02 (reason bounds); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and API-P4-013 (Platform administration, right C, errors 401, 403, 409, 422, 503); Architecture v5 slide 14 P4 IN/OUT lines (authorise, me/permissions, doa-limits, masking-policies; events none on the input side); ownership map (no incident api row).
area: Break-glass access: incident binding, parameters and rights
proposed: Confirm the incident register and its contract with the security administrator before wave 4, seed the two parameter codes in the parameters catalogue, and record the read right beside the activation right in TSD P4 v3 T6.1.

title: The end and read operations, the two schema shapes and the payload of the grant are specified by no source
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2, API-P4-013); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 14 and 42; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-006)
description: (a) Only the activation has a published row: API-P4-013 POST /admin/break-glass-grants names the request BreakGlassActivation and the response BreakGlassGrant but fixes no field list, and the end and read operations have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, so their paths, their rights and their answer shapes are this revision's own decision. (b) The state vocabulary of a grant, the break-glass marker and the identity of the approve reference on the grant are named by no schema. (c) The mapping of a refusal to an HTTP status is not stated: the legacy story gives MSG-P4-004 for an active window and MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-001 for rights, and the activation row adds 409 and 422 without a condition list. (d) The deprecation window of a published field and the retention of the contract fakes are not stated.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 (API-P4-013 is the only break-glass row; no end and no read operation) and T-A.2 (Request BreakGlassActivation, Response BreakGlassGrant, no schema); ownership map api list (POST /admin/break-glass-grants only); legacy RWB-AD-006 Endpoints (GET /admin/access-log only) and Validation and messages (MSG-P4-004); Architecture v5 slide 42 (additive change within major version 1).
proposed: Freeze the three operations, the two schemas and the state vocabulary in the contract baseline, and add the end and read rows to TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A before the wave 4 harness runs.

title: The grant table, its columns, its field ids, its retention and its partition are specified by no source
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.0, T3.1, T4); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 20 and 29; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-006)
description: (a) No grant table exists in TSD P4 v4 T3.1, which declares role, permission, delegation_limit, masking_rule, role_conflict, lov_value and partner_user, and the ownership map has no row for one, so the table name, its columns and its keys are this key's own working decision. (b) No BR Field ID is recorded for any grant column, while the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary fixes the ids of every other P4 field. (c) The retention period, the retention class and the partition granularity of the grant are unset: DL26 is open for retention, so both are parameter rows and the table is not partitioned by this story. (d) The settle of an expired grant (the point at which a row becomes ENDED) and the exact grantee login name are not fixed by any source.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (tables list; no grant table) and T3.0 (standard record columns); ownership map tables list (role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict, delegation_limit; no grant table) and the ruling on library objects ASM-A6-tables-8; TSD P4 v3 T-B (DL26 open for retention); Architecture v5 slide 29 (one login per service, rwb_case shown).
area: Break-glass access: data model and retention
proposed: Confirm break_glass_grant, its columns and its one-active-grant constraint with the security administrator, set the retention period at DL26 with Compliance, and record the login grant in the platform schema baseline.
